**A2 CP-A2b MIRROR PHASE VALIDATED (gitlab.com): full governance chain green live; meta-lesson — infra premieres fail in LAYERS, the self-diagnostic message turns each into a 1-hour fix**

What: CP-A2b MIRROR PHASE VALIDATED on the public gitlab.com mirror (reviewer verdict, 3rd run). MR-compliant = 8/8 Passed — issue-link GREEN exercised the ENTIRE chain in one line: live-API MR body → M1 wide closing-keyword vocab → runtime-provider dispatch (#14) → issueView over direct API v4 (#12) → resolver `:`→`::` → issue's `status::approved` → base-branch addendum on the default branch. MR-non-compliant = issue-link Failed + the other 7 Passed → surgical red + mechanical block via "Pipelines must succeed" = rung 1 GitLab OPERATIONAL.

The layers surfaced across the iteration (each run peeled one):
1. include: — the fragment resolved (ADR-0018 opt-in dogfooded live).
2. IMAGE — #13: node:20 lacks glob in `node --test` → node:22.
3. LOADER/body — case A (operator error: literal `#<IID>` placeholder) proved the ci-context loader reads the MR body via live API; the self-diagnostic message (null-body vs no-ref) discriminated it.
4. DISPATCH — #14: defaultFetchIssue used config provider (github) not runtime ctx.provider (gitlab) → ran `gh` on a GitLab issue.

META-LESSON (ratified): infrastructure PREMIERES fail in LAYERS — an include is not "done" when it resolves; each layer (image, context, dispatch, verb transport) is a separate first-contact failure. The SELF-DIAGNOSTIC MESSAGE (name the tool + status + which stage failed) is what converts each layer from a blind-guess cycle into a ~1-hour fix. It paid off on THREE consecutive findings (#12 case-A, #14 wrong-provider, and the null-body/no-ref split). Corollary: injectable-seam test suites prove LOGIC but NOT that the default impl runs in the target environment — a live smoke against a real (even public-mirror) instance is irreplaceable for infra premieres.

Status: A2 fixture + mirror validated. #231 STAYS OPEN — remaining: CP-A2b SCIT phase (env-specifics smoke: CE version, corporate proxy, self-hosted runners, new endpoint) when the human restores access. That is the ONLY thing between A2 and total closure. Mirror MRs + test/* branches can be closed/deleted (evidence captured in cp-a2b-runbook.md Results). Findings this arc: [[findings/12-gitlab-issueview-glab-ci]], [[findings/13-node20-glob-node-test-ci]], [[findings/14-getvcs-config-vs-runtime-provider]]. Next planning: A3 (GitLab provider verbs, closes m3) vs D2 (auto-revert, awaits human triage).
